title: Hyp Local Stream Perf
objective: Eliminate public genus-2 local-factor materialization overhead using lazy packed records and bulk construction without changing exact stream semantics.

handoff.summary: Added bounded, exact rational_local_coefficient_chunks with immutable (prime, coefficients, backend) rows; adapted public polynomial chunks to standard PolynomialElement objects with lazy packed integer storage; made LocalDataRecord polynomial construction lazy; and capped the duplicate interval stream cache at 256 entries. On quiet bench-1 at limit 100000 (three repetitions), medians were 1.733s packed traversal, 2.695s coefficient chunks (1.555x packed), 3.052s public polynomial chunks (1.761x packed), 5.614s lazy-record coefficient traversal, and 6.275s record polynomial traversal, with a 444481536-byte maximum sequential-process RSS. Public polynomial materialization improved 33.97x from the recorded 103.678s baseline while preserving digest 2c71e4b3f978c930f135267cd98dfb072b952e1432c0ef90e1aa831931512894 and checksum (9588, 454396502, 31923, 459539912).
risks: The 444481536-byte RSS is the maximum resident size of one sequential multi-mode benchmark process, so it includes retained runtime/native state and is not an isolated per-mode allocation delta.
Rich LocalDataRecord statistics remain inherently more expensive than coefficient-only traversal (5.614s versus 2.695s at 100000), although polynomial construction is deferred until requested.

The CoWasm/WASI toolchain was unavailable in this worktree, so browser runtime parity was not rerun locally; architecture:check, including the Wasm capability audit, passed, and the implementation uses the standard baselib packed polynomial representation with an ordinary-construction fallback.
next_steps: Consume rational_local_coefficient_chunks in GlobalCoefficientPrefix.through() with the agreed ImportError/NotImplementedError fallback to the public local_data path.
Run the existing local_lpolynomials browser/Wasm parity case on a prepared CoWasm toolchain and retain platform-matrix receipts on linux-arm64, windows-x64, and macos-arm64.
